title: Dependence-Aware Proof for the Missing-Difference Algorithm
summary: The paper heuristically derives constant success for the fast-convolution missing-difference algorithm at the claimed complexity; a rigorous proof under fixed-sum counter dependence remains open.

formal_statement.body: Can one give a rigorous dependence-aware proof that the fast-convolution missing-difference algorithm succeeds with probability $\Omega(1)$ using $O(n\cdot 2^{4n/3})$ XORed values, equivalently using two balanced lists of size $O(\sqrt{n}\cdot 2^{2n/3})$ each? The proof must account for the fact that the counter variables $X_c$ are not independent but obey a fixed-sum relation, replacing the existing heuristic that this dependence weakens asymptotically and that the induced covariances are negative.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of the fast-convolution missing-difference algorithm with fixed-sum-dependent counters.
parameters: n — asymptotic size parameter governing the XORed-value and balanced-list bounds
X_c — counters indexed by c whose dependence drives the proof gap
scope.unresolved_remainder: Give a rigorous dependence-aware proof of constant success at the claimed XORed-value and balanced-list complexities, replacing the asymptotic negative-covariance heuristic.

citations.label: The Missing Difference Problem, and Its Applications to Counter Mode Encryption

progress.summary: The source derives the stated bound using an independence approximation, then concedes that the counters are tied by a fixed-sum relation. It offers asymptotic and negative-covariance intuition rather than a rigorous proof.
citation_labels: Gaëtan Leurent et al., The Missing Difference Problem, and Its Applications to Counter Mode Encryption
